outcomes: read a client request and write down the task, the finished result, the sources, the deadline in your time, the limits and the open questions
tell which gaps you can fill yourself and which only the client can answer
decide whether to go ahead, ask first, or pass a decision to the client
plan the work in a sensible order and follow a client's checklist or process
check your work against the request before you say it's done, and handle revisions without breaking what was right

fit_check.text: When a client sends a request, I can list everything they asked for, including the limits and the deadline in my time.
I can tell which missing details I can find myself and which only the client can answer.
I know when to go ahead, when to ask first, and when a decision isn't mine to make.
I can break a task into steps and follow a client's checklist or process.
Before I say a task is done, I check it against what was asked.

lessons.title: Reading a Client Request

anchor.subject: Trade fair contacts
anchor.label: Email from Grace Tan: Trade fair contacts
body: Hi Ana! Hope your week's off to a good start. We just got back from the spring trade fair and it was so busy. We met a lot of new stockists (stores that sell our pieces), and I'd like to follow up with them before they forget us. Could you put their contacts into our Stockist Tracker sheet? The business cards are scanned in the "Trade Fair Cards" folder in Drive, 23 cards. Add each one as a new row with name, shop, city, email and phone. Some cards have no email; just leave that blank, don't go searching for it. Please don't change the existing rows, Mark uses them for deliveries. Tag the new ones somehow so I can tell they're from the fair. I need it before my call with our distributor on Thursday at 10 AM my time. Thanks!

thread.title: Grace Tan
thread.label: Chat thread: three messages from Grace Tan

messages.text: Ana, a wholesale buyer from Lumen Home wants to see our best sellers. Can you put together a folder with photos of our 12 best-selling products?

Use the white-background photos only, the lifestyle ones aren't ready. Also make a short list in a Doc: product name, photo file name, and wholesale price. The wholesale prices are in column D of the Price List, not the retail ones.
She flies into LA on Monday, so I'd like to send it to her Sunday night my time. Don't send it to her yourself, I'll do that.

l1a4.label: Activity
l1a4.title: Do or Background?
l1a4.intro: Grace sent this chat. For each sentence, choose Do if it asks you to do something (including "don't" and "only"), or Background if it only gives news, a reason, or a greeting.

items.q: "Hi Ana, quick one before the weekend."
items.good: A greeting. Nothing to do yet.
items.try: This is only a greeting. Nothing is asked.

items.q: "Our holiday orders doubled last year, so we're preparing earlier this time."
items.good: It explains why, but doesn't ask for anything.
items.try: It sounds urgent, but it only explains why Grace is preparing early. No task is in this sentence.

items.q: "Could you make a copy of last year's Holiday Orders sheet and name it Holiday Orders 2026?"
items.good: A request, even though it's written as a question.
items.try: "Could you…?" is a polite way to ask for work. This is the main task.

items.q: "Last year the sheet got confusing because people typed dates in different ways."
items.good: It's the reason for the next sentence.
items.try: This describes a past problem. The instruction about it comes in the next sentence.

items.q: "So in the new one, please use one date format only: YYYY-MM-DD."
items.good: "Please use one date format only" is an instruction, and a limit.
items.try: It follows a reason, but "please use… only" asks you to do something. It's a limit for your Task Card.

items.q: "Joy might ask you about it; she's new and still learning our system."
items.good: Useful to know, but nothing is asked of you.
items.try: It sounds like you might need to act, but Grace doesn't ask for anything here.

items.q: "Don't delete anything from last year's sheet; we still need it for taxes."
items.good: "Don't delete anything" is a limit. The tax part is the reason.
items.try: "Don't delete anything" is something you must follow, so it counts as Do. The reason is attached, but the limit is the instruction.

items.q: "Thanks so much, you've been a big help this month!"
items.good: A kind closing. Nothing to do.
items.try: This is a thank-you. Nothing is asked.

l1a5.label: Activity
l1a5.title: Which Result Matches?
l1a5.intro: The task tells you what to do. The finished result is what should exist at the end. Choose the result that matches each request.

items.q: Grace: "Add the three new suppliers to the Supplier Contacts sheet with name, email and phone. Keep the list in A–Z order by name."
feedback: All three are there with every field, but they're at the bottom. Grace asked for A–Z order, and that's part of the finished result.
Everything Grace asked: all three suppliers, all three fields, and A–Z order.
The order is right, but the phone numbers are missing for the new suppliers. Grace asked for name, email and phone.

items.q: Grace: "Save the signed Luntian contract as a PDF in the Contracts folder, named Luntian-Contract-2026."
feedback: Right name and folder, but it's a Word file. Grace asked for a PDF.
A PDF, but the name isn't the one Grace gave, and it's in the Suppliers folder instead of Contracts.
Right type and folder, but not the name Grace asked for. She may search for "Luntian-Contract-2026" later.
Right type, right name, right folder. That's the finished result.

l1a5b.label: Activity
l1a5b.title: Convert the Deadline
l1a5b.intro: All of these are from Grace in Portland, in October.

items.q: Grace: "I need it by Thursday 10 AM my time." When is that in the Philippines?
feedback: That's Grace's time, not yours. Add 15 hours: Friday 1 AM in the Philippines.
That subtracts the 15 hours. Portland is behind the Philippines, so you add: Friday 1 AM.
Thursday 10 AM + 15 hours = Friday 1 AM. Plan to finish Thursday evening your time.
The day moves forward, and the hour changes too: 10 AM + 15 hours = 1 AM Friday.

items.q: It's 9 PM on Tuesday in the Philippines when Grace writes: "Can you send it by tomorrow morning?" When is that for you?
options: Late Wednesday night to early Thursday, Philippine time
feedback: When Grace writes, it's 6 AM Tuesday in Portland, so her "tomorrow morning" is Wednesday morning there. 9 AM Wednesday in Portland is 12 AM Thursday for you.
That's your tomorrow. Grace means her tomorrow: Wednesday morning in Portland, which is around midnight Wednesday night for you.
It's 6 AM Tuesday for Grace when she writes, so "tomorrow" is Wednesday there. You have until about midnight Wednesday night your time.
That's a few hours too late. Wednesday morning in Portland is late Wednesday night to early Thursday for you.

items.q: Grace: "EOD Friday, please." No time is given. What do you write under Deadline?
options: Friday 11:59 PM, Philippine time, since EOD means end of day
About Saturday 8 AM Philippine time (5 PM Friday hers), and add "exact EOD time?" to Open questions
Friday 5 PM, Philippine time, since that's a normal end of workday
Any time on Friday, since no hour was given, so there's nothing to note
feedback: EOD usually means the end of the client's workday, not yours. If it's 5 PM Friday in Portland, that's Saturday 8 AM for you. And because "EOD" isn't an exact time, note it as an open question.
EOD usually means around 5 PM her time, which is Saturday 8 AM for you. Since she didn't say an exact time, you also note it as an open question.
That's the end of your workday, not Grace's. Her 5 PM Friday is Saturday 8 AM for you, and the exact time should go under Open questions.
A missing hour is something to note, not ignore. Write down your best reading (about Saturday 8 AM your time) and add the exact time to Open questions.

items.q: Grace: "I need it before my call with the distributor on Monday." What do you write under Deadline?
options: Monday 11:59 PM Portland time, the last minute of Monday
Monday end of day, Philippine time
No deadline, because Grace didn't give an exact time
Before a Monday call at an unknown time. Note it, and add "What time is the call?" to Open questions
feedback: The call happens during Monday, and the work is needed before it. The end of Monday is too late.
Monday evening for you is still early Monday in Portland, but you don't know when the call is. Note the missing call time.
There is a deadline: before the Monday call. You just don't know the time yet. Write the deadline down, and add the call time to Open questions.
The deadline is real, and its exact time is missing. Both belong on the Task Card.

lumen.label: Practice
lumen.title: Your Task Card
lumen.note_heading: My Task Card: Lumen Home photos
lumen.intro_html:
Now a new request, with no labels. It's a Friday afternoon in October in Portland. Grace sends three chat messages:

{{mock:thread}}

Wholesale price: the lower price for stores that buy many pieces to resell.

Fill in your Task Card. Short notes are fine, in English or Taglish. Your answers are saved in this browser.
lumen.check_intro: Compare each part with the model. Mark each one. It's for you only.

fields.label: Task
fields.placeholder: Everything Grace asked you to do
fields.model: Make a folder with photos of the 12 best-selling products, and a Doc listing each one's product name, photo file name and wholesale price
fields.check: Did you include both the folder and the Doc?

fields.label: Finished result
fields.placeholder: What will exist when you're done
fields.model: One folder with 12 white-background product photos, plus one Doc with a 3-column list for the same 12 products, ready for Grace to send
fields.check: Did you say 12, white-background, and what goes in the Doc?

fields.label: Sources
fields.placeholder: Files or information you'll work from
fields.model: The white-background product photos; the Price List, column D (wholesale); information on which products are the best sellers
fields.check: Did you name column D of the Price List, not just "the price list"?

fields.label: Deadline
fields.placeholder: In Philippine time, plus Grace's words
fields.model: Sunday night Portland time = about Monday midday in the Philippines (for example, Sunday 9 PM there = Monday 12 PM here). "Night" isn't an exact time
fields.check: Did you convert it to Philippine time, and note that "night" isn't exact?

fields.label: Limits
fields.model: White-background photos only. Wholesale prices only (column D, not retail). Don't send it to the buyer; Grace will
fields.check: Did you get all three, including don't send it?

fields.label: Open questions
fields.placeholder: What the messages don't tell you
fields.model: Which 12 are the best sellers, and where does that information come from? What time on Sunday night? (Smaller: what to name the folder and the Doc?)
fields.check: Did you include which 12 are the best sellers?

closing.critical_missed: These two cause the most trouble in real work. A missed limit can mean sending something Grace said not to send. A deadline read in the wrong time zone can mean finishing a day late. Read the three messages once more, looking only for times and for "don't", "only" and "not". Then update your card.
closing.other_missed: You caught the deadline and the limits, which are the hardest parts. Check the part you missed against the model. Often it's the second task in a later message, or a detail like "column D".
closing.all_got: That's a complete Task Card. You'll use this same card in the next lesson.

lumen.after_html: In Lessons 2 and 3 you'll decide what to do about your open questions. If one does need to go to Grace, the wording comes from Communication & Professionalism, Lesson 3.

next_preview: Your Task Card has open questions. Some you can answer yourself, and some only the client can answer.
Lesson 2 starts with the Task Card you just made and sorts its open questions: the ones you already have an answer for, the ones you can find, and the ones that need Grace.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check the reading habits from this lesson.

questions.q: Grace writes: "The last VA was slow, so I'm hoping this goes faster. Please rename the files by date." Which part is the instruction?
questions.explain: Only the last sentence asks for work. The first two are background: how Grace feels and why.

questions.q: Where on the Task Card does "Don't change the existing rows" belong?
questions.explain: It's a "don't", something you must follow while you work. That's a limit.

questions.q: A client in New York is 12 hours behind the Philippines in October. They ask for "Wednesday 9 AM my time". When is that for you?
questions.explain: Add 12 hours: Wednesday 9 AM there is Wednesday 9 PM in the Philippines.

Here's the Task Card you made for Grace's Lumen Home request.

{{carry:l1card}}

{{mock:shared}}

And a message from Grace in the same chat last Thursday:

{{mock:lastthu}}

For each open question on your card, who has the answer?

items.q: Which 12 products are the best sellers?
feedback: Grace didn't list them in her messages. But the Best Sellers tab in Sales by Product – Sep 2026 does, so you can find it yourself.
The Best Sellers tab in Sales by Product – Sep 2026 lists them. No need to ask Grace.
Grace knows, but so does her sales sheet: the Best Sellers tab in Sales by Product – Sep 2026. Asking her would cost her time for something you can look up.

items.q: What time on Sunday night does Grace need it?
feedback: You have "Sunday night", but not a time. Nothing in the messages or files says when she plans to send it.
None of the files or messages say when Grace plans to send it to the buyer. Only she knows.

items.q: What should the folder and the Doc be called?
feedback: Grace told you last week: Buyer – Purpose – Month. So: Lumen Home – Best Sellers – Oct.
You don't need to look anywhere. It's in the chat already: "Buyer – Purpose – Month", from last Thursday.

l2b3.label: Activity
l2b3.title: Sort the Gaps
l2b3.intro: A new request from Grace. Read it, look at what you can see, then sort each gap.

mocks.subject: October stock count
mocks.label: Email from Grace Tan: October stock count
body: Hi Ana! Please send the October stock count to Mark at the warehouse by Wednesday. Use the same template as last month, and include the three new mugs (Moss, Clay and Sky). Thanks!

messages.text: The new Portland shop opened last week!

items.q: Which items are "the new mugs"?
feedback: They're named in the email: Moss, Clay and Sky.
No need to look anywhere. Grace named them in the email: Moss, Clay and Sky.
Grace already answered this in the email: Moss, Clay and Sky.

items.q: Should the count include stock at the new Portland shop, or only the warehouse?
feedback: The email doesn't say. September's template only has a warehouse column, and the shop opened after that.
September's count was before the shop opened, so it can't tell you. No file decides this. It's Grace's choice.
September's count only had the warehouse, and the shop is new. Nothing you can see decides it, so it's Grace's call.

items.q: Where's last month's template?
feedback: Grace didn't attach it. But it's one click away in the Stock Counts folder: Stock Count – September.
It's in the Stock Counts folder: Stock Count – September.
You can find it without asking: Stock Count – September, in the Stock Counts folder.

items.q: Should damaged items be counted as stock?
feedback: The email doesn't mention damaged items, and neither does the template.
Look at the template again: Item, Warehouse qty, Notes. There's no rule for damaged items anywhere you can see.
The template has no rule about damaged items, and the email doesn't say. That's Grace's decision.

items.q: What's Mark's email address?
feedback: It isn't in Grace's email. But it's in the Team Contacts sheet.
It's in the Team Contacts sheet: mark@harborhill.co.
No need to ask Grace. It's in the Team Contacts sheet.

items.q: When is "by Wednesday" in your time?
feedback: You can work this out yourself, as in Lesson 1: Wednesday in Portland runs into Thursday for you. Grace didn't give an exact time, though, so that part goes on your list for her.
There's nothing to look up. You can convert it yourself, as in Lesson 1. Only the exact time is missing, and that part is for Grace.
Converting "Wednesday" to your time is something you can do yourself, as in Lesson 1. Only the exact time is missing, and that part is for Grace.

l2b4.label: Activity
l2b4.title: Unfamiliar or Unclear?
l2b4.intro: Each pair looks alike. Look for the one detail that makes them different.

items.q: Grace: "Export last month's orders as a CSV." You've never heard of a CSV.
options: Unfamiliar: I can learn it or look it up
feedback: Everything about the task is stated. CSV is a file type you can look up in a minute.
Grace said which orders and which format. You just don't know the format yet, and that's something you can look up.

items.q: Grace: "Export the orders for the accountant." She doesn't say which months, and there are two years of orders.
options: Unfamiliar: I can learn it or look it up
feedback: You know how to export, but not which orders. Two years or one month is a choice someone has to make, and it isn't you.
Which orders? Grace hasn't said, and no file decides it.

items.q: Grace: "Use our brand colours for the flyer." Recent posts use two different greens, and there's no brand guide anywhere in the shared Drive.
options: Unfamiliar: I can learn it or look it up
feedback: You could look around, but the files disagree and nothing written down settles it.
Two greens and no guide. Nothing settles which one is the brand colour.

items.q: Grace: "Use our brand colours for the flyer." There's a Brand Guide Doc in the shared Drive.
options: Unfamiliar: I can learn it or look it up
feedback: Same request as before, but this time the colours are written down in the Brand Guide.
Same request as the one before, but this time there's a Brand Guide. You don't know the colours yet; you can look them up.

items.q: Grace: "Request a courier pickup for Friday." The shop and the warehouse are at different addresses, and Grace doesn't say which.
options: Unfamiliar: I can learn it or look it up
feedback: Knowing how to request a pickup doesn't help if you don't know where from. The address is missing.
Pick up from where? The request doesn't say, and both addresses are possible.

items.q: Grace: "Request a courier pickup from the warehouse for Friday." You've never requested one, but the courier's website has a pickup request page.
options: Unfamiliar: I can learn it or look it up
feedback: Where and when are both stated. You just haven't done it before, and the courier's page shows how.
This time Grace said where: the warehouse. Everything else is learnable from the courier's page.

l2b5.label: Activity
l2b5.title: Find the Mismatch
l2b5.intro: Sometimes the instruction and the files don't agree, or two instructions say different things. For each one, choose what's actually wrong.

items.q: What doesn't match?

mocks.subject: Trade fair contacts
mocks.label: Part of Grace's email from Lesson 1
body: The business cards are scanned in the "Trade Fair Cards" folder in Drive, 23 cards.

mocks.label: Trade Fair Cards folder with 21 files

options: Some cards have no email address.
The folder has 21 scans, but Grace said 23 cards.
The folder is in Grace's Drive, not yours.
The scans are images, not a spreadsheet.
feedback: True, and Grace already said what to do about that. The mismatch is the count: she said 23 cards, and the folder has 21.
Grace's number and the folder disagree. Write it down with both sources. You'll decide what to do about it in Lesson 3.
That's normal for a client's files. The mismatch is the count: 23 in the email, 21 in the folder.
That's expected for scanned business cards. The mismatch is the count: 23 in the email, 21 in the folder.

items.q: What doesn't match?

messages.text: The wholesale prices are in column D of the Price List, not the retail ones.

mocks.name: Price List
mocks.label: Price List sheet with columns A to E

options: Some prices are higher than others.
The sheet has five columns instead of four.
The sheet was last changed on September 28.
Column D is labelled Retail. Wholesale is in column E.
feedback: That's normal: products cost different amounts. Look at the column headers.
The number of columns isn't the issue. Look at what column D is called.
The date isn't the problem. Look at column D's header: it says Retail.
Grace said "column D" for wholesale, but the sheet says D is Retail. Note both sources.

items.q: What doesn't match?

messages.text: For the new photos, put the product name first, like we used to.

options: Grace's new message and the File Naming note give different name orders.
The File Naming note uses dashes in the date.
Grace's message doesn't say how many photos there are.
The File Naming note is a Doc, not a Sheet.
feedback: One says date first, the other says product name first. Note both, and which is newer.
Dashes are just the format. The two instructions disagree about what comes first.
That might be a gap, but it isn't the mismatch. The note says date first; Grace now says product name first.
The file type doesn't matter. The note and the message give different name orders.

items.q: What doesn't match?

mocks.subject: Price list
mocks.label: Grace's email with a linked file
Drive search results for Price List

options: The linked file has "(1)" in its name.
The email didn't say which columns to use.
The linked file isn't Grace's Price List: it has a different owner and is over two years old.
The file is a Sheet, not a PDF.
feedback: That's one clue, but not the whole problem. Look at who owns it and when it was last changed.
That might be a gap, but it isn't the mismatch. Look at the linked file's owner and date.
Grace's Price List is owned by her and was updated on September 28. The linked one is from another account, in 2024.
The file type isn't the issue. Look at the owner and the date.

lumensort.label: Practice
lumensort.title: Sort Your Open Questions
lumensort.intro_html:
Back to the Lumen Home request. You've now opened the files, and found two things:

{{mock:photos10}}{{mock:pricehead}}
  • The white-background folder has photos for 10 of the 12 best sellers. The other two only have lifestyle photos.
  • In the Price List, column D is Retail and column E is Wholesale.

Sort everything you still need to know into four lists. Short notes are fine, in English or Taglish. Your answers are saved in this browser.
lumensort.check_intro: Compare each list with the model. Mark each one. It's for you only.

fields.label: I already have it
fields.placeholder: What you already know, and where it came from
fields.model: Folder and Doc names: Lumen Home – Best Sellers – Oct (Grace's message last Thursday). Deadline: Sunday night Portland = about Monday midday for you (Lesson 1)
fields.check: Did you include the folder name, and where it came from?

fields.label: I can find it myself
fields.placeholder: What you'll look up, and where
fields.model: Which 12 are the best sellers: the Best Sellers tab in Sales by Product – Sep 2026
fields.check: Did you put "which 12" here, with the Best Sellers tab?

fields.label: Only Grace can answer
fields.placeholder: What only Grace can decide or tell you
fields.model: What time on Sunday night she needs it. What to do about the two best sellers without white-background photos: use a lifestyle photo, leave them out, or wait for new photos?
fields.check: Did you include both the Sunday time and what to do about the two missing photos?

fields.label: Mismatches I found
fields.placeholder: What doesn't match, and the two sources
fields.model: Grace said wholesale prices are in column D, but in the Price List column D is Retail and column E is Wholesale. Grace asked for 12 white-background photos; only 10 exist
fields.check: Did you include both the column D/E problem and the 10-of-12 photos?

closing.critical_missed: These two lists matter most. A missed mismatch can mean putting retail prices in a wholesale list. A missed question can mean deciding something that was Grace's to decide. Notice that the missing photos belong in both lists: the fact (only 10 of 12) is a mismatch, and what to do about it is Grace's call. Add what you missed.
closing.other_missed: You caught the mismatches and the questions for Grace, which are the hardest parts. Check the first two lists against the model. Often it's a name Grace already gave you, or a file you could open.
closing.all_got: That's a complete list. In the next lesson, you'll decide what to do about each item under Only Grace can answer and Mismatches I found.

lumensort.after_html: In Lesson 3 you'll decide what to do about each question and mismatch. If something does need to go to Grace, the wording comes from Communication & Professionalism, Lesson 3.

next_preview: You now have a list of what only Grace can answer, and the mismatches you found. Some of them block the work. Some don't.

quick_check.purpose: A few questions to check the sorting from this lesson.

questions.q: Grace asks you to "use the same layout as the September report". The September report is in the shared Drive. Who has the answer to "what layout?"
questions.explain: The September report is in the shared Drive. Open it and you'll see the layout.

questions.q: Grace's request mentions "SKU". You don't know what that means, but everything else is clear. What kind of gap is it?
options: Unfamiliar: you can look it up
A question only Grace can answer
questions.explain: Nothing is missing from the instruction. SKU is a common term you can look up.

questions.q: Grace writes "Thursday, October 16". In 2026, October 16 is a Friday. What is this?
options: A mismatch: the day and the date disagree
A typo you can safely change to Thursday the 15th
Nothing to note, since the date is what counts
A question only the accountant can answer
questions.explain: The day and the date point to different days. Write it down as a mismatch; deciding what to do comes in Lesson 3.

lessons.title: Checking Your Work and Handling Revisions
